title: Effect Size and Statistical Power Analysis
description: Quantification of practical significance and computation of sample size requirements.
conditions: Planning experimental sample sizes (A/B testing, clinical trials)
Interpreting p-values on very large or very small sample sizes
recommended_methods: Cohen's d for standardized difference between two group means
Eta-squared and Partial Eta-squared for ANOVA effect sizes
selection_rules: Never declare findings significant based solely on p < 0.05; always report effect size (e.g. Cohen's d)
Benchmark Cohen's d: 0.20 small, 0.50 medium, 0.80 large practical effect
Before launching an A/B experiment, calculate minimum detectable effect (MDE) and required sample size
limitations: Retrospective post-hoc power calculations based on observed p-values are mathematically redundant and misleading
Standardized effect sizes depend on sample homogeneity and cannot always be compared across different populations
source: Cohen (1988) Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences
